path_rules.description: For the QuakeWorld game (manifest selector "-quake"/"q1"), FTE's gamemode_info[] entry defines the base game directory set as id1/, qw/, and *fte/ (the asterisk marks a private gamedir). When the manifest selector resolves, FS_Manifest_SetDefaultSettings copies the gamepath array into the manifest. FS_ChangeGame later iterates gamepath[] calling FS_AddGameDirectory for each base dir; each call pushes the dir to the head of com_searchpaths via FS_AddPathHandle. Effective lookup order is *fte > qw > id1 (last added is highest precedence in the LIFO stack).
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_Manifest_ReadMem(const char * fname, const char * basedir, const char * data)

path_rules.description: com_searchpaths is a singly-linked list traversed head-first. FS_FLocateFile walks `for (search = com_searchpaths ; search ; search = search->next)` and returns the first FindFile match. Every FS_AddPathHandle call inserts at the head, so the most recently added directory or archive is checked first.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_FLocateFile(const char * filename, unsigned int lflags, flocation_t * loc)

path_rules.description: After mounting all base gamepath entries (id1, qw, *fte for QW), FS_ChangeGame snapshots com_searchpaths into com_base_searchpaths. Subsequent `gamedir` swaps unwind paths above this snapshot but preserve the base stack -- so id1, qw, *fte always remain mounted.

FS_RegisterDefaultFileSystems registers archive backends in this order: dz, pak, pk3, pk4, pkz, pkx, iwd, apk, zip, kpf. Later- registered kinds are scanned later in FS_AddDataFiles, and each scan's matches push onto the LIFO searchpath stack. Net effect for QW: pk4 > pk3 > pak. Quake 1 / QuakeWorld installs rarely use pk4; in practice this collapses to pk3 > pak.

Within a game directory FS_AddDataFiles loads pak0.<ext>, pak1.<ext>, pak2.<ext>, ... in numeric-ascending order until one is missing. Because each is pushed to the head of com_searchpaths on load, higher-numbered paks end up earlier in lookup order. Effect: pak1.pak overrides pak0.pak for same-name entries. Same loop runs per archive kind (pak, pk3, pk4).
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddDataFiles(searchpath_t ** oldpaths, const char * purepath, const char * logicalpath, searchpath_t * search, unsigned int pflags, unsigned int loadstuff)

path_rules.description: If a file named `pak.lst` exists in the game directory, FS_AddDataFiles parses it for an explicit pak-load ordering before the numbered-pak scan. Names listed there are loaded by FS_AddSingleDataFile in file order. Unlike ezQuake's pak.lst (which suppresses the wildcard scan entirely), FTE's pak.lst is additive: numbered + manifest + wildcard scans all still run after the pak.lst entries.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddDataFiles(searchpath_t ** oldpaths, const char * purepath, const char * logicalpath, searchpath_t * search, unsigned int pflags, unsigned int loadstuff)

path_rules.description: After loading the numbered pakN.<ext> series and any manifest- declared packages, FS_AddDataFiles enumerates `*.<ext>` in the same directory and pushes each match to the head of com_searchpaths. Wildcard-discovered archives sit higher on the stack than numbered paks of the same extension and so take precedence.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddDataFiles(searchpath_t ** oldpaths, const char * purepath, const char * logicalpath, searchpath_t * search, unsigned int pflags, unsigned int loadstuff)

path_rules.description: FS_AddGameDirectory pushes the directory itself onto com_searchpaths (via FS_AddPathHandle). FS_AddPathHandle then triggers FS_AddDataFiles which pushes archives within that directory on top. Net effect: archives override loose files in the same directory.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddPathHandle(searchpath_t ** oldpaths, const char * purepath, const char * logicalpath, searchpathfuncs_t * handle, const char * prefix, unsigned int flags, unsigned int loadstuff)

path_rules.description: `gamedir <mod>` and `-game <mod>` both route through FS_ChangeGame, which loads a fresh manifest (or alters the existing one) and rebuilds the searchpath stack. Old searchpaths above com_base_searchpaths are freed; the base stack survives. The new mod directory is mounted via FS_AddGameDirectory on top of the base.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_ChangeGame(ftemanifest_t * man, qboolean allowreloadconfigs, qboolean allowbasedirchange)

path_rules.description: After mounting a mod dir, lookups for assets missing in the mod fall through to the next searchpath entries -- which are the base stack (qw, id1 for QW). This works automatically because FS_FLocateFile's LIFO walk continues past head when FindFile misses; mod directory was pushed last so it's consulted first, but absent matches fall through to the next entry.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_FLocateFile(const char * filename, unsigned int lflags, flocation_t * loc)

path_rules.description: `-basedir <path>` overrides the auto-detected base directory (where id1/, qw/, and *fte/ are searched). Checked during init; when present, base game directories are resolved relative to this value.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_ChangeGame(ftemanifest_t * man, qboolean allowreloadconfigs, qboolean allowbasedirchange)

path_rules.description: `-game <mod>` (or `+gamedir <mod>` at the console) calls FS_ChangeGame to mount the named mod gamedir on top of the base stack. Equivalent to running `gamedir <mod>` immediately after init.

`-quake` selects FTE's QuakeWorld game manifest (id1/qw/*fte gamepath set, QUAKEPROT protocol, q1 mode key). FTE supports multiple game manifests via cmdline selectors (-quake, -quake2, -quake3, -hexen2, etc.); -quake is the QW-relevant one. The manifest's installation string is matched against gamemode_info[i].argname inside FS_Manifest_SetDefaultSettings, which then copies the gamepath set into the manifest.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_Manifest_ReadMem(const char * fname, const char * basedir, const char * data)
